The second review of the opening proposal ([drafts/2026-10-10-opening/history/OPENING-V7-PROPOSAL.md](../../../../../../drafts/2026-10-10-opening/history/OPENING-V7-PROPOSAL.md), "New work that would allow stronger claims", item 2) ranked as the direct answer to an outside critique, that the theory proves the rules of its own invented universe and then assumes that ours runs the same way, an instance theorem for a formalism defined outside the theory, with each premise derived or characterised exactly. None existed.

**The choice.** Two candidates were named: discrete Petri nets, or chemical reaction networks with whole-number counts, and finite Markov kernels on counts. Place/transition nets are taken. Their commitments are the spine's own: discrete steps, whole-number amounts, and change as what is taken and given; so the map is the identity on what each says, and nothing is approximated. They are a standard formalism of concurrency, chemistry and biology, defined long before this repository, with known laws (P-invariants, siphons, termination by a linear ranking) against which the instance can be checked. A Markov kernel assigns probabilities, which are not whole-number amounts; an instance would need a second correspondence, a law over distributions or over sample paths. Its pathwise half is already this one: every sample path of a stochastic reaction network's jump chain fires one enabled reaction at a time, so it is a sequential firing sequence of the underlying net, and the laws below hold on every path (a modelling remark, not in the Lean).

**The net, by its own rules.** `Net T P` holds `pre f p` and `post f p`. A step is a list of transitions, repetition allowed (a multiset: step semantics); it is enabled at a marking where it consumes from each place at most what the place holds; firing removes what it consumes and adds what it produces; a schedule is a firing sequence from `M₀` where each step is enabled at the marking reached. A net is pure where no transition consumes from and produces into one place; a schedule is sequential where at most one transition fires at a time. None of these definitions uses the spine. Weights `y` on the places read tokens in units, as a P-semiflow does.

**The map.** In units `y`, the net's exchange law takes `y p * pre f p` and gives `y p * post f p` whatever has stood (`Net.law`); the flow along a schedule has the schedule's steps as the formations taking part (`Net.flow`); the web reads the markings in units, a transition active exactly where it fires, requiring and drawing on the places it consumes from at its weighted multiplicity (`Net.web`). Read as one world (`Net.world`), places and transitions are the relata: a transition stands at one, the structure of the net, and a place at its weighted marking, active while marked.

**What holds by the net's definitions.**
- The law reads what has stood (`Net.law_nonanticipating`, by `rfl`: it reads nothing), and the course it generates along a schedule is the net's flow (`Net.course_eq`, by `rfl`). Along a firing sequence its levels are the markings in units (`Net.Fires.levels_eq`).
- **Balance is the firing rule.** Along a firing sequence the flow balances the markings in any units (`Net.Fires.balances`), and with every weight positive it balances exactly where the schedule is a firing sequence (`Net.balances_iff`): a step not enabled breaks balance at the place it overdraws, because the marking floors at zero.
- **Feasibility.** Enabling gives the law's feasibility (`Net.Fires.feasible`), so `ExchangeLaw.course_balances_iff` applies (`Net.Fires.course_balances`). Feasibility is weaker: it lets a step use what it produces in the same step. It is enabling exactly for pure nets fired one transition at a time (`Net.fires_iff_feasible`), and both conditions are needed: a catalyst, one transition consuming and producing a token at an empty place, is feasible and does not fire (`Net.catalyst_feasible_not_fires`), and so is a concurrent step of a pure net in which a sink uses what a source produces (`Net.relay_feasible_not_fires`). The spine's feasibility is the firing rule with token reuse within a step.
- **The tying premises.** Only active transitions give (`Net.acting`), only active transitions take and only from what they draw on (`Net.taking`), and along a firing sequence activity needs support (`Net.Fires.dependent`): enabling a step bounds each transition's multiplicity at each place by the marking.

**What holds exactly under a named property of the net.**
- **Dissipation is a strict P-subinvariant.** A transition loses in units `y` over the places where it produces no more weighted tokens than it consumes, and fewer when it consumes any (`Net.Loses`; implied by `y·post < y·pre`, a strict P-subinvariant, `Net.Loses.of_lt`). For finitely many places listed once, with equality of places decided, the flow is dissipative exactly where every transition it fires loses (`Net.dissipative_iff`): over any family closed across a step the totals are those over all places (`Net.total_eq_closed`). The sign form admits null transitions, consuming and producing nothing weighted; a strict P-subinvariant excludes transitions with no weighted input.
- **Enclosure** holds at every step of a net with finitely many places (`Net.enclosed`, and `Net.world_enclosed` for the world).
- **Census and embodiment** hold of the world with finitely many transitions (`Net.world_counted`, `Net.world_embodied`), and the world balances and dissipates where the flow does (`Net.Fires.world_balanced`, `Net.world_dissipative`).

**The laws, for nets.** Along a firing sequence of a net with finitely many places whose fired transitions lose:
- a step raising one place's weighted marking lowers another's (`Net.rise_with_fall`, from `Flow.rise_with_fall`; in tokens, `Net.rise_with_fall_tokens`);
- the transitions consuming anything, fired over the first `n` steps, number at most the initial weighted token count (`Net.takers_within`, from `Flow.Balances.takers_within`), the classical bound of a firing sequence by a decreasing linear ranking `y·M`; so firing them does not recur (`Net.taking_not_recurring`);
- that the marking stops changing from some step on cannot be refuted (`Net.change_stops_unrefuted`, from `Flow.change_stops_unrefuted_around`; in tokens with positive weights, `Net.marking_stops_unrefuted`), and, with finitely many transitions, every premise of `World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed` holds of the world, so that from some step on no place is emptied or newly marked cannot be refuted (`Net.rests_unrefuted`). Naming the step is a principle of omniscience, as on the spine: the schedule is any function.
- **The siphon law is the joint-excess law.** A place is gated at `m` where every transition producing into it consumes at least `m` tokens from it. Where a place is gated at `m`, `n` steps of a firing sequence each consuming from it more than they produce, starting below `n + m`, leave every transition consuming at least `m` from it dead from then on (`Net.gated_ends`, from `Flow.joint_excess_ends`). With `m = 1` and `n = 0`, an empty place every producer of which consumes it stays empty and every transition consuming it is dead (`Net.siphon_empty`): the one-place case of the classical law that an emptied siphon stays empty, which in reaction networks is the extinction of an autocatalytic species (`A + X → 2X`).

**Where a premise fails, the law fails.** The conservative cycle (`Net.cycle`), one token moved back and forth between two places, fires forever; its world balances, has a census, is embodied and enclosed at every step (`Net.cycle_premises`), and is not dissipative (`Net.cycle_not_dissipative`); its marking changes at every step (`Net.cycle_changes`, the negation of the flow form's conclusion) and its world never rests (`Net.cycle_never_rests`). The fed place (`Net.fed`): a place emptied by its consumer is refilled by a transition that does not consume it; its flow balances, one step of joint excess starts below `1 + 1`, the place is not gated, and the consumer is active two steps later, so the conclusion of `Flow.joint_excess_ends` fails (`Net.fed_refills`).

**The integration.** The first connectivity check found 3 of the module's 73 theorems standing apart from the base: the fed place's firing and its refilling, stated of the net alone, and the relay's purity. The fed place's failure was then stated on the flow and the web, as the failure of `Flow.joint_excess_ends`'s conclusion with its other hypotheses holding, and the purity joined to the relay's feasible course; now 0 of 73 stand apart. On this tree there are 59 dependency components, 20 spine theorems outside the main one, and 161 statements on both families.

**What this changes.** For one standard formalism defined outside the theory, the spine's premises are not stipulations about an invented universe: balance and the tying premises are the net's firing rule, read; dissipation is a named, checkable property of a net (a strict P-subinvariant on what fires); enclosure is its finiteness. The laws of rising with falling, of bounded taking, of rest and of joint excess are then theorems about every net with that property, and they coincide with laws Petri-net theory already knows (termination by a decreasing linear ranking, the siphon property), which is a check that the instance reads the nets correctly. Where the property fails, as in a conservative cycle, the law fails, so the premise is doing work. What remains a correspondence is the step from a physical system to a net: which places, transitions and weights it has.

*Reading* [AI reading]. The opening's `[^proof]` note carries, citing the record: "The laws hold, as theorems, of every Petri net with finitely many places, along every firing sequence: its flow balances its markings exactly because the firing rule is respected; and where each transition it fires consumes more weighted tokens than it produces (a strict P-subinvariant), a place gains tokens only as another loses them, the firings that consume number at most the tokens at the start, and that its marking comes to rest cannot be refuted, while an emptied place that only its own consumers replenish stays empty. The conservative cycle, which loses nothing, never rests." Its body takes the third-pass edit (pp), agreed with the v7 opening ([proposal, third pass](../../../../../../drafts/2026-10-10-opening/history/OPENING-V7-PROPOSAL.md#third-pass-edits-for-results-verified-and-queued-19-october)): after "can check for itself", "Nor are these laws of a world made for them alone: they hold, as theorems, of systems defined without them, every place/transition net among them, each premise following from the net's own firing rule or stated as a property of the net that anyone can check." The world form's reading of a transition as standing at one is the AI's; the flow form needs no such reading.

**Not done.** Inhibitor arcs, capacities, and timed, stochastic and continuous nets; the stochastic laws (expected counts, fluctuations), which T1 studies for dissipation; siphons of more than one place; nets with infinitely many places, where enclosure is a property of the step and not of the net; deciding reachability or coverability; an independent review.

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean: every theorem named above is in the module with the hypotheses given here, the counterexamples are computed by `rfl` and kernel reduction, and no match with overlapping patterns or library lemma bringing `propext` is used (the cycle's and the world's exchange are written as nested exhaustive matches for that reason).
